Complete layouts of task, runqueue, domain, group, bucket, affinity, and node structures.
Class specific selection, enqueue, dequeue, affinity, preemption, and clock behaviors.

findings.text: Placement and affinity services choose a destination processor for a task and allow forced replacement of eligibility information. Selection consults class specific logic when several processors are permitted, otherwise uses affinity data, and widens the search when the first choice is ineligible.

Queue and wakeup entries coordinate transitions between sleeping and runnable conditions. They refresh timing, maintain utilization and pressure accounts, delegate to class handlers, manage core participation, and publish runnable state with tracing.

Eligibility requires affinity membership plus role sensitive liveness. Ordinary threads need active state, migration restricted contexts and per processor kernel threads need online state, other kernel threads avoid dying processors. Assignment publishes runqueue association before processor identity with ordering visible to remote lockers.

Callers hold priority inheritance protection during placement. Affinity replacement, wakeup queuing, utilization updates, and pressure group mutation execute under runqueue protection, with additional change guards, per processor sequence sections, atomic exchange, and read side sections for polling work.

Pressure accounting distinguishes restore, delayed migration, runnable migration, and fresh wakeup. Group mutation adjusts per condition counters with underflow detection, derives some and full masks for input output, memory, processor, and idle activity, accumulates durations, and schedules averaging and polling work.

Utilization control keeps per task requested and effective values with bucket identity and activity indication, and per runqueue aggregates with buckets holding totals and maxima plus idle retention. Effective values respect system defaults and group restrictions, with inert alternates when the feature is disabled.

Wakeup of an already queued task refreshes timing, requeues delayed entities, checks for proxy return, requests preemption when queued but not resident, then marks runnable. Proxy return clears blocked relationships under protection and reblocks in waking condition when processors differ.

Failure to locate any eligible processor is fatal. Counter underflow and inconsistent flag transitions emit one time errors with a sticky defect marker. Delayed handling without expected migration marking triggers a one time warning.

Wakeup statistics are collected only when globally enabled, separating local and remote cases, attributing remote cases to domain hierarchy, and counting migration, total, and synchronous events. Disabled builds provide inert behavior with no accounting.

Core scheduling advances a per core sequence on membership change, ignores delayed entities, tracks participation through node linkage and cookie presence, and requests rescheduling when the last task leaves forced idle. Scheduling information records first queued time when previously unset, with inert alternates.
